Normalise reference-bounded numeric findings for CTAS

Transform_Range.Rd

Consumes the long-format frame produced by Standardize_Domain() and normalises value against the reference bounds low/high so results from different tests are comparable on the same scale. The original values are preserved as extra columns (original_value, lower, upper, original_category).

Usage

Transform_Range(
  dfInput,
  strPrefix = "RANGE",
  strFallbackPrefix = "NUM",
  dMaxShareMissingRange = 0.5
)

Arguments

dfInput

data.frame Long-format output of Standardize_Domain() with the reference range columns low/high.

strPrefix

character Prefix for the generated parameter_id.

strFallbackPrefix

character Prefix for fields switched to raw numeric values.

dMaxShareMissingRange

numeric Maximum share of observed values per field without a usable reference range before the field switches to raw numeric values.

Value

data.frame in the CTAS long-format vocabulary carrying the extra original_value/lower/upper/original_category columns. parameter_id is prefixed with strPrefix (or strFallbackPrefix); parameter_category_2 keeps the raw input parameter_id so ctasapp can stitch this metric with sibling metrics on the same field.

Details

Rows are never dropped within a field: rows with a missing value or an unusable reference range keep result = NA so CTAS can apply its missingness threshold. Fields where more than dMaxShareMissingRange of the observed values lack a usable range are emitted unnormalised as parameter_category_3 = "numeric" with the strFallbackPrefix prefix. Fields without any observed value are kept with result = NA and listed in a message, so they still anchor source data in ctasapp.

Data Specification

dfInput must include:

  • subject_id - Subject identifier.

  • parameter_id - Raw test code (e.g. LBTESTCD).

  • parameter_name - Human-readable test label.

  • parameter_category_1 - Domain label (e.g. "Labs").

  • parameter_category_2 - Field anchor; retained as the grouping key.

  • visit, visitnum - Visit label and numeric ordering.

  • value, low, high - Numeric result and reference bounds.
